summary: T3-04 passes every acceptance criterion. Both listed checks exit 0 (82 tests passed; ruff and mypy strict clean). The tests are real and compare against independent references. The diagonal-lag and isotropic-rule decisions are documented and surfaced in the story notes. One consequence needs human attention: on the 90 m grid no diagonal is supported at any configured lag. I did not re-run the failing-first run at c59d0a5. The implementation reads as written, with no zero-fill and no randomness.

checks.criterion: Failing test run recorded before implementation (test_terrain_structure.py fails first)
checks.evidence: Commit order is c59d0a5 (tests only) then f9bf03d (terrain.py). The story notes in prd.json record ImportError: cannot import name 'terrain' at c59d0a5. I did not re-run that commit.

checks.criterion: Plane test: per-direction nu equals |L|*|grad . u| at 270/360/540/720/1080 m, rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12
checks.evidence: test_plane_axis_nu_is_lag_times_gradient_along_the_axis (test_terrain_structure.py:188) uses LAGS from config and close() with RTOL 1e-10 and ATOL 1e-12. It passed. Diagonal planes are tested with diagonal lags at :208, with NE and NW told apart at :233.

checks.criterion: Sinusoid test: x matches sqrt(2)*A*|sin(pi*L/lambda)| within a derived finite-window bound; y gives 0
checks.evidence: The bound 1/(M|sin(2 pi D/lam)|) is derived in the comment at test_terrain_structure.py:248-260. Tests at :281 (limit within bound), :297 (closed-form sum), :312 (y is a supported 0.0) and :324 (convergence) passed.

checks.criterion: Nodata: pairs need both cells valid; masked never zero; hole equals hand-removed pairs; no valid pairs is unsupported, not 0
checks.evidence: Brute-force pair loop (:117) compared at :438. Filler tests with NaN, inf, 0 and 1e30 at :451. Masked-array mask at :472. Checkerboard, single column and all-nodata cases at :485-545, which assert reason set and nu_m None. The implementation _pair_differences (terrain.py:337) ANDs both cell masks; no zero fill.

checks.criterion: Diagonal lag rule documented and tested for 270 m and 360 m; reason diagonal_lag_not_on_grid; surfaced to human
checks.evidence: Rule is in the terrain.py:18-28 docstring and implemented at :314-326. test_configured_lags_are_not_on_the_diagonal_grid_at_90_m (:347) asserts the reason for 270 m and 360 m. It is recorded as decision (1) in the prd.json notes.

checks.criterion: Isotropic rule documented, an explicit parameter recorded in the output, per-direction values unchanged
checks.evidence: isotropic_rule is a required argument (terrain.py:217), stored in StructureFunction.isotropic_rule and IsotropicNu.rule. test_isotropic_rule_is_recorded_and_leaves_per_direction_values_unchanged (:609) passed. The rule is documented at terrain.py:39-48.

checks.criterion: Pure numpy float64, no randomness, mypy --strict passes
checks.evidence: make check exit 0: ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed, mypy 'Success: no issues found in 12 source files'. An AST no-randomness test exists at :776, and terrain.py imports only numpy and the stdlib.
Exit 0; ruff, format and mypy all clean

checks.criterion: Scope: changed paths within the story's files list
checks.evidence: The code changes are only terrain.py and test_terrain_structure.py. The other touched paths are Ralph bookkeeping (prd.json state and notes, progress.txt). config/run.yaml is untouched.

findings.claim: On the 90 m grid with the configured lags (270, 360, 540, 720, 1080 m) both diagonals are unsupported, so the isotropic summary rests on the two axes only.
findings.evidence: This follows from the documented rule: 270 m would need k=2.12 diagonal cells. test_configured_lags_are_not_on_the_diagonal_grid_at_90_m asserts it. The story notes surface it as human decision (1); the PRD 6.3 text and the T3-05 consumer should be settled before relying on the isotropic value.

findings.claim: The module-level filterwarnings('error') applies to all tests in the file, so a numpy RuntimeWarning in the tests fails them. This is intended and not a defect.
findings.evidence: pytestmark at line 58; all 82 tests passed with it active.
